heroHeadline: Putin Says War 'Coming to an End' — But Breaks Ceasefire Again on Day 2; Russia Stalls 1,000-for-1,000 Prisoner Exchange
heroSubtitle: On May 10, 2026 — Day 2 of the Trump-brokered 3-day ceasefire — Putin declared Russia's war on Ukraine is 'coming to an end' and offered to meet Zelensky in a third country, but only after a final peace deal is already agreed. Meanwhile, Russia continued breaking the ceasefire: 780 strikes hit 33 settlements in Zaporizhzhia (1 killed, 3 wounded); Kharkiv took a residential drone hit (including two 8-year-old boys); 7 were wounded in Kherson. Ukraine's Air Force intercepted all 27 overnight drones. 147 front-line clashes were recorded. Russia simultaneously stalled the landmark 1,000-for-1,000 POW exchange — with Putin claiming Ukraine was 'not ready,' contradicting both Zelensky's and Trump's announcements. Ukraine called it a Russian violation of pledges made to the United States. Day 1,536 of the full-scale invasion.
